# Requirements Document - Fleet Reliability API (v1.0)
*Portfolio project; all data is SYNTHETIC (generated by Project 1).*

## 1. Purpose and scope
Give analysts and other applications (BI tools, scripts, internal apps) controlled, documented programmatic access to fleet reliability data: vehicles, failures, work orders, mileage-derived KPIs, the mileage audit and the data-quality log. **Out of scope:** user management, a web UI, writing mileage or work-order data, real-time telemetry.

## 2. Stakeholders and users
| Role | Need |
|---|---|
| Reliability analyst | Pull KPIs and failures into Excel/Power BI/Python |
| Ridership/mileage analyst | Check mileage reconciliation and data-quality flags |
| Maintenance planner | Look up a vehicle's failures and linked work orders; log a failure |
| IT support | Simple deployment, health check, clear errors, logs |

## 3. Functional requirements
| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| FR-1 | List and filter vehicles (type, division) with paging | Must |
| FR-2 | Retrieve one vehicle with failure count and total km | Must |
| FR-3 | List failures filtered by date range, system, severity, vehicle type, division, vehicle | Must |
| FR-4 | Retrieve one failure with its work orders | Must |
| FR-5 | Create a failure record with validation (known vehicle, valid date not in future/before in-service, valid system and severity) | Must |
| FR-6 | Reject duplicate failures (same vehicle, date, system) with 409 | Must |
| FR-7 | Reliability KPIs (failures/100k km, MDBF, road calls) grouped by vehicle type, division or month, with month-range filter | Must |
| FR-8 | Availability KPI by division or month | Must |
| FR-9 | Expose mileage-audit flags and the data-quality error log, filterable | Should |
| FR-10 | List work orders incl. orphan filter | Should |
| FR-11 | Publish an OpenAPI specification | Should |
| FR-12 | Health endpoint without authentication | Should |

## 4. Non-functional requirements
| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| NFR-1 Security | Every endpoint except `/health` and `/docs/*` needs a valid `X-API-Key`; key comes from environment, never source control (the default `dev-key` is for local use only). All SQL parameterised; dynamic identifiers whitelisted |
| NFR-2 Consistency | KPI results must equal Project 1's published KPI tables (automated test) |
| NFR-3 Errors | JSON errors `{error:{code,message,details}}` with correct HTTP status (400/401/404/405/409/422/500); no stack traces to clients |
| NFR-4 Performance | Paged lists (default 50, max 500); typical responses < 500 ms on the demo dataset (~58k mileage rows) |
| NFR-5 Maintainability | Single module, tests runnable with the standard library (`unittest`), config by environment variables |
| NFR-6 Data integrity | Foreign keys enabled; writes limited to failures; DB file backed up before deployment |

## 5. Data
Source: SQLite `data/api.db` = Project 1 `fleet.db` plus `error_log` and `mileage_audit` tables (`scripts/prepare_db.py`). Entities: vehicles, daily_mileage, failures, work_orders, reported_division_km.

## 6. Assumptions, constraints, risks
- SQLite is adequate for the demo; a production move to SQL Server/PostgreSQL would change only the connection layer and a few SQL functions (`substr`, boolean sums).
- One shared API key (no per-user identity or audit trail) - acceptable for a prototype; production would use OAuth2/SSO and an audit log.
- POST writes to the same DB the KPIs read, so new failures change KPIs by design.
- Concurrency: SQLite allows one writer at a time; fine at this scale.

## 7. Acceptance criteria
All 15 automated tests pass (`python -m unittest discover -s tests`); OpenAPI spec loads in Swagger Editor; sample requests in the User Guide return the documented responses.

## 8. Traceability
FR-1/2 -> test_vehicle_*; FR-3 -> test_failures_filters; FR-5/6 -> test_create_failure_*; FR-7 -> test_kpi_*; FR-8 -> test_availability; FR-9/10 -> test_audit_and_dq, test_work_orders_orphans; NFR-1 -> test_auth_required, test_sql_injection_is_inert; NFR-2 -> test_kpi_matches_project1; NFR-3 -> test_unknown_route_json.
